page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.medium is an x86_64 virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include any local storage or GPU hardware accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.e3.medium exhibits modest processing and memory performance. Its single-core stress-ng CPU performance score of 1102.08 and multi-core score of 2162.17 fall into the lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth tests show 156.12 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, which drops to 17.2 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, indicating potential bottlenecks during large data transfers. Geekbench testing aligns with these results, showing a single-core score of 981.0 and a multi-core score of 1743.0.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not demand intense CPU throughput. However, the tradeoff is its lower overall processing speed, as evidenced by a Passmark database operations score of 554.18 and a Redis SET throughput of 2.52 million operations per second.

The ecs.e3.medium is best suited for lightweight memory-optimized workloads. These include small-scale database hosting, caching layers, basic web serving with a static throughput of 2.49 GB/sec, and simple background utility tasks that require a larger memory footprint than standard general-purpose instances but can tolerate lower CPU performance.
